clue.text: Gordon initially mocked Cameron''s reinvention as "ordinary"

indicators.note: a reinvention remakes something in a new form, so the collected letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows, so only that one letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of mocked
taken as written; the possessive is just surface

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown sneers at David Cameron's political makeover as nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: Two party leaders of 2008 supply nearly all the letters; Gordon Brown and David Cameron were then Prime Minister and Opposition leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Common-or-garden is an idiom for something everyday and unremarkable, so it can stand for plain ordinary.

clue.text: Moderates gain ground in pages of newspaper

parts.note: in politics the centre is the moderate grouping between left and right
to spread is to extend or gain ground

explanation.surface: A political report: moderate parties make headway in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre spread is the pair of facing pages in the middle of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Chap in charge is ludicrously busy

parts.note: a chap is a man
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The man running things is absurdly overworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frantic, frenzied activity, so it suits someone absurdly busy.

clue.text: Dutiful marshal's not brave

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the S of the apostrophe ending
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dutiful officer in charge of order turns out to be a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal looks like the officer the sentence is about, but it is a verb telling you to put the letters, including the S after it, in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant can mean diligent in keeping rules or religious duties, which makes it a synonym of dutiful.

clue.text: Was against page of newspaper having positive content

indicators.note: having something as content means holding it inside, so one piece sits within the other
content is what a thing holds within it, so the following piece is placed inside the page

parts.note: an op-ed is the page opposite the editorial, carrying opinion pieces
POS is the abbreviation for positive

explanation.surface: Someone objected to an upbeat article in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' and 'content' together signal containment: the positive piece is what the newspaper page holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposed to something is to be against it, so the past form matches was against.

clue.text: Relative with a daughter absent somewhere in Spain

indicators.note: something absent is missing, so that letter is taken out of what precedes it

parts.note: a grandad is a relative
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family member and his daughter are away somewhere in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain, home of the Alhambra palace.

clue.text: In summer, oasts get very hot

indicators.note: In tells you the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rural fact: in summer the hop-drying kilns heat up.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasts are kilns for drying hops, a familiar sight in Kent in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast can mean to be uncomfortably hot, as people roast in a heatwave.

clue.text: English medic is absorbed by inner working of glands

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: what is absorbed by something is taken inside it, so one piece goes within another
something working is in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a doc is a doctor

explanation.surface: An English doctor is engrossed in how glands function internally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner working of glands' reads as one phrase, but 'working' rearranges the word before it and 'of glands' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Endocrine is the adjective for the ductless glands that secrete hormones into the blood.

clue.text: Northern girl playing cards

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for northern
Ines is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from the north is busy with a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like a verb describing the girl, but it belongs with cards in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Each suit in a pack holds a nine, so the four nines are particular playing cards.

clue.text: Notices president has way with oddballs

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for president
La is the abbreviation for Lane, a kind of road or way
a card is an eccentric or comic person

explanation.surface: Someone observes that the president gets on well with eccentrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notices' reads like a verb, but it is the plural noun defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Placards are posted signs or boards bearing public announcements, which are notices.

clue.text: Rover of old sets off on hazardous journey around cape

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the earlier phrase is wrapped about the following piece

parts.note: to venture out is to set off on a risky trip
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: An old wanderer embarks on a dangerous voyage round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover suggests a wanderer, but Rovers were the senior section of the Scouts, later replaced by Venture Scouts, themselves since renamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture Scouts were the older Scouting section, the successor to Rover Scouts, and are now historical.

clue.text: With reference to guy's accounts

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to
a guy is a rope holding a tent, so a cord; the 's makes it plural

explanation.surface: A note in a letter referring to some man's financial books.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy is not a man here but a guy rope, the cord that steadies a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Records and accounts are both written narratives or registers of what happened, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: It might be the essential substance of particles

indicators.note: the essential substance is the core, so only the inner part of the next word survives, with its ends stripped

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters stripped away

explanation.surface: Sounds like a physics question about what matter is fundamentally made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is not just a word in the sentence: it is the example being defined, the definite article in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, so the definition names an example of the answer.

clue.text: A lass's wild dance

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman's dancing is uninhibited.
explanation.walkthrough: Lass is a northern British word for a girl or young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American partner dance, so it is a kind of dance.

clue.text: Liberal, for example, is slow to bring in a new law

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
e.g. stands for for example
taken as written
a clock that is slow is running late

explanation.surface: A complaint that a Liberal politician drags their feet over new legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, so introducing a new law is the act itself.

clue.text: Marlowe, perhaps having shot artist, runs away

parts.note: a dram is a small shot of spirits

indicators.note: whatever goes away is no longer there, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A crime story: Marlowe shoots a painter and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlowe could be Raymond Chandler's detective, which suits the shooting, but here it is Christopher Marlowe the Elizabethan playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe wrote plays such as Doctor Faustus, so he is an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Harmonise with me on squeeze box

parts.note: to accord is to agree or harmonise
the speaker's me becomes I
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to sing in harmony with a squeezebox player.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeeze box is a slang name for the accordion, played by squeezing the bellows.

clue.text: This rogue could become honest

indicators.note: the words could turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hopeful line about a villain going straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright and virtuous, which is close to honest.

clue.text: Get head round religious idea

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the first piece wraps about the next

parts.note: onion is British slang for the head, as in use your onion
pi is short for pious, so religious

explanation.surface: Advice to grasp a spiritual concept: get your head round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your head round' is an idiom for understanding, but head is split off and replaced by a slang word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief someone holds, so it is a kind of idea.

clue.text: Fancy cups set out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in place, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lays out the elegant china for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an adjective for the cups, but it is a verb meaning to guess.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to imagine or believe it, and to suspect is likewise to believe without proof.

clue.text: Applaud revolutionary monarch

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An instruction to clap for a king who led a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to shout approval, which is a way of applauding them.

clue.text: Idiot finally gave thug first-rate weapon

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: finally refers to the end, so only the closing letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of gave
the closing letter of thug
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A fool finally handed a hoodlum a top-quality weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid key printed the variant ASSAGAI, but the wordplay gives E as the fourth letter, which no other answer checks.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: German, oddly, has one large cherished ambition

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A German, strangely, holds a big dream dear.
explanation.definitionFit: From the quest for the Holy Grail, a grail is any long-sought goal or ambition.

clue.text: They copied documents, making second copies to include note

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to crib is to copy, and cribs are copies
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Office drudgery: someone reproduced paperwork, adding a memo to the duplicates.
explanation.walkthrough: A crib is a copied answer, as a student cribs from a neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Before printing, scribes were professional copyists who wrote out documents and books by hand.

clue.text: Supporter starts to voice word of approval

indicators.note: the starts are the opening part, so only the beginning of the next word is kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan begins to shout praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Supporter suggests a fan, but it is the crossword's favourite undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation shouted to praise a performer, so it is a cry of approval.

clue.text: Ecstasy is found in assembly

indicators.note: something found in another thing lies inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a parade is a formal assembly, as of troops
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sounds like a report of drugs discovered at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy suggests the drug, but here it is the feeling of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is used figuratively for a state of supreme happiness or bliss, which is ecstasy.

clue.text: Girl has house in northwestern state

parts.note: Ida is a girl's name
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A woman owns a home in the American northwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the Pacific Northwest region, bordering Canada.

clue.text: City market stall's reduced footwear

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Wellington, capital city of New Zealand
a booth is a stall at a market or fair

explanation.surface: A shop in some city market has cut its prices.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wellington boot, or welly, is the British name for a rubber rain boot; 'reduced' sounds like a sale but trims a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wellington boot is a waterproof rubber boot, so it is an item of footwear.
